# Accuracy, currentness and learning notes

Source statements remain descriptions of the registered guide. Original source pages and every stated condition must travel with the rule. The cover edition and the older contents-footer label are both retained in provenance; no handbook effective date is inferred. Administrative and immigration-document descriptions require current issuer confirmation before they are relied on for an individual application. The passport-stamp paragraph leaves the exact boundary case unstated, so that outcome is not invented.
Memory cue, authored product policy: “Identity, originals, signatures.” Use the cue to retrieve the complete cited requirements.
Terminology: primary and secondary identify the guide’s separate evidence lists; those labels do not create an additional document requirement.
Misconception to avoid: a notarized photocopy is equivalent to a certified record copy. The registered rule distinguishes them.
